This does work. Use Silver polish (any metal polish).

Just a couple drops, rub it with a dry, clean sift cloth in small circles over the entire disc.

Let it dry cloudy. (Takes about 3-5 minutes.)

Use another dry, soft cloth and polish it, again in small circles until it is clear and shiny again.

90% of the time, this fixed it - although not forever.

Back in the 90's, when you had to constantly swap out game discs, you in variably ruined the surface popping them in and out all the time. I went through the wife's silver polish just to keep playing the original Baldur's Gate!

That should be easy to fix. I used to use toothpaste to buff out the scratches in my cd's. The data is actually on the backside of the top layer of the cd. The laser shines through the layer of protective plastic on the bottom to read it.

If the scratches are on the label side, well then the disc is fucked. The aluminized layer is just beneath the label with only a thin clear lacquer layer to protect it. The shiny side can be fixed but the label side cannot.
